text:
maria: Heads-up — canary rollout of base-image v2026.03 with nvidia-container-toolkit 1.12 landed on 3/12 us-west-2 pool and a handful of pods are failing to start with libcuda mount errors.
chris: saw it on the dashboard, ~12 nodes with CrashLoopBackOff, looks like only the p4d and a few 3090 nodes.
anya: error snippet from kubelet logs: `container_linux.go:348: starting container process caused: chdir to cwd ("/workspace") set in config.json failed: no such file or directory` — but the real failure is earlier: `/usr/local/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`
kurt: the toolkit 1.12 package moved host lib mounts from /usr/lib/nvidia to /usr/local/nvidia by default, we changed the image to rely on /usr/lib earlier. mismatch => mount path missing inside container.
chris: is this new behavior documented? I skimmed the release notes and there was a line about "host lib path normalization" but nothing on the default path.
anya: confirmed with a repro node: `docker run --rm --gpus all --privileged my-test-image:canary ls -l /usr/local/nvidia || ls -l /usr/lib/nvidia` shows only /usr/lib/nvidia present on host. toolkit tries to bind /usr/local/nvidia -> container but host doesn't have it so container drops the mount and binary can't find libcuda.
maria: consequence: pods using the gpu-device-plugin fail early which cascades to our autoscaler marking nodes underutilized and then evicting pods, cluster churn. costly and noisy.
sre-bot: Incident alert: 12 impacted nodes, 48 affected pods, increased pod churn in us-west-2-gpu-pool-3.
kurt: quick mitigation: patch DaemonSet for toolkit config to add NVLIBS_PATH=/usr/lib/nvidia and set hostPath mounts for both /usr/lib/nvidia and /usr/local/nvidia as optional. I'll draft a kubectl patch.
chris: please also throttle the rollout, rollback the base-image tag on node pool, we don't want this to hit other regions.
anya: minimal patch I ran on a repro node: ```
# on node
sudo ln -s /usr/lib/nvidia /usr/local/nvidia
# restart kubelet / containerd
sudo systemctl restart containerd
```
anya: that worked to allow containers to start, but creating a symlink on thousands of nodes manually is terrible.
maria: options: 1) rollback base-image in the nodepool CI -> safest 2) patch the toolkit DaemonSet to mount both paths -> medium 3) push config change to the toolkit package to fallback to existing host path -> longer.
kurt: I pushed a limited canary rollback for 20% of nodes in the pool and paused the remainder. opening a change ticket to rollback the node image for the rest.
chris: need to confirm impact on Dedicated and Private fleets — any nodes in eu-west or ap-south already updated?
maria: only us-west-2 had the automation trigger; other regions are pending, thanks to the staged deploy.
sre-bot: Note: cost impact estimate — churn + restarts ~ 60 node-minutes wasted so far, rough $180 per hour equivalent for the affected window.
anya: diagnostics notes: containerd event log shows: `failed to mount "libnvidia-ml.so" from host: path not found` and `toolkit: host lib path not present, skipping bind` which then leads to loader error `libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file` inside container.
kurt: I'm preparing an emergency patch to the toolkit DaemonSet. Patch will add hostPath mounts for /usr/lib/nvidia and /usr/local/nvidia and set them optional with readOnly. Also set env NVLIBS_PATHS="/usr/local/nvidia:/usr/lib/nvidia" and fallback logic in entrypoint. Rolling to canary nodes first.
maria: please include a test in the rollout checklist to verify host path existence and a post-install probe that runs `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` inside a test container.
chris: I'll notify partners and customer-facing teams — low risk but noisy. any ETA on patch?
kurt: creating PR now, should be in canary within 20m, full rollback if any failure.
anya: FYI this also impacts one-off debug shells where engineers exec into containers; without host lib mounts the shell can't start GPU libs, makes debugging harder.
maria: long term we should pin a canonical host lib path in our base images and vendor a compatibility-layer that checks /usr/lib and /usr/local and symlinks if necessary during node boot. add to infra roadmap.
sre-bot: Action items: rollback schedule recorded, toolkit DS patch in PR, create node boot script ticket, update deploy playbook to verify host lib paths.
chris: thanks team — keep updates in this thread, I'll update #incidents if the rollback changes. :thumbsup:
